top.line: AgentiCCells' first offering: a public website as an atomic cell, anchored at £500.
top.para: Ordered, queued, built by agents, steered from the customer's browser with a key, and handed over.

in-short.line: The offering, steering by key, two modes, public sites, capacity, and the people.

why.line: A website is the easiest way to feel what an agentic team can do.
why.para: agenticcells.com is the product in miniature.

atomic.line: Every offering is a one-off, owned atomic cell; the ladder reads as organisms.
atomic.para: £500 anchors a fair price with room for partners.

flow.line: Order, queue, build, preview, key, steer, handover: seven steps without the founder.
flow.para: Built from pieces we already have: agentic teams, person keys, vault lanes.

modes.line: No-touch, on our accounts; or their own, with GitHub and Claude.
modes.para: £500 for the first, from £1,500 for the second.

control.line: What we sell is control of the site through its agents.
control.para: A key and a lane, or the console.

people.line: A queue and a staff: Angelo Leggio, Silvio Switha and José Bota implement; Vicky Wang manages.
people.para: The first of a network of partners.

dogfood.line: Our own projects become cells on agenticcells.app, with me as editor.
dogfood.para: Each tests the flow and becomes an example.

limits.line: A proposal; public sites only; our accounts during the build; Claude and GitHub for the second mode.

sources.line: My own thinking and earlier articles.
sources.para: With links to the company and the key and lane articles.
